File details

Compare your well logs

Add and manage wells

Choose Add wells and select several LAS files, or drop files onto the page. New files are added to the current workspace. The attached 746PO example is included in this HTML and loads automatically. Parsing, plotting, and exports happen in your browser.

Check a well to include it in the comparison. Select its name to view that file’s metadata under Active well details. The remove button unloads a well from this workspace; it does not change the original LAS file. Loaded files are held in memory for this browser session.

Two comparison layouts

Side by side groups tracks by well. Selected curves appear in the same order for each well. A curve missing from one file has an empty track.

Overlay curves puts matching curves from the visible wells in a shared track. The legend identifies wells by color. Both layouts use one synchronized depth window and shared horizontal limits for each matched curve.

Choose matching curves and scales

The curve list covers the loaded wells. Curves match by mnemonic and unit, ignoring case and spacing. Curves with different units remain separate. Duplicate curve names are kept distinct. The viewer does not guess aliases or convert measurement units.

Check a curve to include it. Click its name to set its shared minimum, maximum, linear or logarithmic scale, horizontal direction, and soft fill. Auto scale uses valid values across the comparison. Zero and negative values are omitted from logarithmic plots but retained in the data and CSV export.

Depth alignment

All visible wells use the same depth axis. Supported metre and foot indices are converted to the first loaded well’s display unit. CSV export keeps both the displayed depth and the original source depth and unit.

Alignment uses the file indices. No formation correlation, depth shift, or datum correction is applied. Wells with incompatible index types or units cannot share this comparison.

↑ / ↓, + / −
Pan or zoom with keyboard focus on the plot. Escape releases the cursor.

Missing data and different sampling

Each well keeps its own samples and sample interval. NULL values remain missing. Plot lines break at missing samples and depth jumps larger than 1.5 times that well’s median positive sample interval. No resampling or interpolation is applied between wells.

Cursor readings use the nearest actual sample separately for each well. Missing curves, missing values, and depths outside a well’s coverage have no reading. Dense plots retain first, last, minimum, and maximum points per screen row; inspection and exports retain numerical resolution.

Exports

PNG exports the visible depth window and current comparison layout with the selected tracks and well labels. The cursor is omitted.

CSV uses a long table: Well, File, Depth, Depth unit, Source depth, Source depth unit, Curve, Curve unit, and Value. It contains the visible wells and selected curves at their original sample depths inside the visible interval. NULL values are empty cells; absent curves do not create invented rows. Duplicate depth samples are retained.

Supported files and limits

Numeric LAS 1.2 and 2.0, WRAP YES or NO, space/tab-delimited rows, scientific notation, D exponents, descending depth, and files without a .las extension are supported. Text may be UTF-8, UTF-16 with a byte-order marker, or Windows-1252. LAS 3.x and malformed tables are reported as errors.

Up to 12 wells may be loaded, with up to 40 rendered tracks. Each input file may be up to 50 MiB, with a total input size of 150 MiB per workspace. Reduce the selected wells or curves, or use the overlay layout, when a side-by-side comparison reaches the track limit.

The included example

Well 746PO has 20,861 samples from 1026.6 to 3112.6 m at 0.1 m intervals. Vp is in m/s, RHOB_INV in g/cm3, and DT_INV in us/m. RHOB_INV begins at 2800.0 m and has seven missing samples at 2892.1–2892.7 m.
